Subject: stan-as-a-service?
To: Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu>, Rob Trangucci <robert.t...@gmail.com>, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com>


Hi guys - 

I've been experimenting a bit with Docker and am thinking of putting together a stan-specific Docker image on top of the official base R one. Just wanted to check in with you guys to make sure this isn't something you've already done? 

Mostly I'm doing this to avoid bit-rot on R packages, etc in the time between sending a paper out and getting it back for revisions or to be able to revisit an old analysis. But I'm also toying with the idea of making a simple stan server that just takes stan code, input data and config options as JSON and sends back model output just to not kill my battery while working remotely.

-Jon

messages.author: 91d53d643859f8d6
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: stan-as-a-service?
parts:
To me the advantage of JSON over protocol buffers is the ease of getting from a webpage or some other front-end API to the server w/JSON, plus you lose the overhead of the protocol buffer compiler.

My original thought was to do a request-reply type interface using RZMQ so that the requesting process (i.e. on my laptop) would block while waiting for the server reply. My primary motivation for doing this would be to preserve the order of a make-based buildchain that looks something like:

raw data -> data munging in R -> run stan model -> post-process stan -> 'compile' to figures & Latex.

-Jon

messages.author: 91d53d643859f8d6
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: stan-as-a-service?
parts:
Yeah - I think JSON would be better for the request end than the reply; agree that it would get very messy/inefficient to be throwing around large output files in JSON.

I think in an ideal world, the reply would be a URL to the traces stored somewhere, e.g. in S3 or just on the server. That way if you had some kind of distributed workflow, you could pass that reference around rather than having a ton of traffic up and down for large output.

One component of this kind of server implementation might also be an efficient database backend for post-processing. For example, one of the things I did like about working with PyMC was the ability to store the output of models in an HDF5 database.

-Jon

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] stan-as-a-service? (server storage, HDF5, streaming)
parts:
The issue in coding output in something like JSON
is how to stream output. The output is a row for
each draw and a column for each value recorded per
draw (parameters, lp__, diagnostics).

1. If we don't stream, it's natural to represent the
data column-wise, perhaps even with structured values.
That makes extract very easy.

This also fits in with Jon's idea to just return a link.
I like this idea. We could conceivably automatically
generate graphical output this way and store it on the
server, too.

Julia is also using HDF5 --- I only heard about it last
week. Anyone think it's worth doing for Stan?

2. If we do stream, we probably want to start by sending
parameter names and dimensions, and then for each draw,
just return a vector. That'd be about the same cost as
for now with CSV. The client could then convert that
back to something with more structure or aggregate a
bunch of draws to implement extract.

We could stream on the back end (server side) to create
the file to return for (1). We can easily stream through
compression.

For (1), we could also compress; that's much harder with
(2) because the data's by column and we couldn't maintain
compression memory across draws without a lot of work (at least
I don't know packages that'll let you do that).

- Bob

messages.author: 91d53d643859f8d6
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] stan-as-a-service? (server storage, HDF5, streaming)
parts:
The only knock on HDF5 is that it can be a bit of a pain to get installed, at least the last time I tried. But once you have it up and going, it's great; pretty close to in-memory speed, much faster to load than from CSV. Plus if this was part of a Stan docker image, the issue of installation wouldn't be a big one.

Also, there's no reason something like this couldn't be compatible with the current CSV-based output, i.e. instead of writing a running model into the DB, just post-process it into it, since the benefit is mostly in access time rather than write time.

It would also make it easy to bundle the input data with the output (a perennial issue at least for me), since it has support for collections of data objects with heterogeneous links. A bit like a NoSQL kind of database but without all the unnecessary features and much, much better compression and access.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] stan-as-a-service? (server storage, HDF5, streaming)
parts:
Write and read are always going to be horrible if
what's being written and read is an ASCII dump in decimal
of an intrinsically binary number. Binary's the only solution.

Usually, the write and read hit from this isn't the bottleneck
in MCMC, but it can come up in optimization, where the I/O eats up
the majority of the time. That's why Marcus has been urging us to
think about binary I/O pretty much as soon as he wrote an efficient
optimizer.

- Bob

On Tuesday, July 21, 2015 at 12:54:23 AM UTC-4, Jeffrey Arnold wrote:
Not as ambitious as the Stan-as-a service, but I put together a few Dockerfiles for rstan (built on top of rstudio) and cmdstan while I was trying to scale out my computing. Here's the repo on github: https://github.com/jrnold/docker-stan

This line in the Dockerfile

'rstan::set_cppo("fast")'        

does not do anything with rstan >= 2.7.0. You should instead execute the R code here

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/wiki/RStan-Getting-Started#configuration

including at the end

cat("\nCC=clang", "CXX=clang++", 
    file = M, sep = "\n", append = TRUE)

I would also put

library(rstan)
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())

into ~/.Rprofile .

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: stan-as-a-service?
parts:
Thanks, I adjusted the Dockerfiles to account for the changes in rstan 2.7.0. But I thought it better to use rstan::rstan_options rather than loading rstan in the Rprofile.

Oops, I forgot that loo is on CRAN. And of course I included loo; loo would not be the one package that I left out.

On Tue, Jul 21, 2015 at 7:51 AM, Jonah <jga...@gmail.com> wrote:
I see that you also included loo. Cool!  If you want you can have it install the loo package from CRAN now, but no big deal as the github version should work fine.

On Tuesday, July 21, 2015 at 12:54:23 AM UTC-4, Jeffrey Arnold wrote:
> Not as ambitious as the Stan-as-a service, but I put together a few Dockerfiles for rstan (built on top of rstudio) and cmdstan while I was trying to scale out my computing. Here's the repo on github: https://github.com/jrnold/docker-stan
>
>
> On Thu, Jul 2, 2015 at 5:53 AM, jzelner <jze...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>
> Yeah - I think JSON would be better for the request end than the reply; agree that it would get very messy/inefficient to be throwing around large output files in JSON.
>
>
>
> I think in an ideal world, the reply would be a URL to the traces stored somewhere, e.g. in S3 or just on the server. That way if you had some kind of distributed workflow, you could pass that reference around rather than having a ton of traffic up and down for large output.
>
>
>
> One component of this kind of server implementation might also be an efficient database backend for post-processing. For example, one of the things I did like about working with PyMC was the ability to store the output of models in an HDF5 database.
>
>
>
>
>
> -Jon
